Lina (Marketing): Quick launch/Q&A ask — we need a reproducible 10k stratified bench for the webinar & blog. Focus: tail latency, multilingual failures, and slide-ready artifacts. Slices: token buckets <32 | 32-256 | 256-1024 | >1024. Langs: en, es, zh, ar, other. Variants: rwd-7b-v1 (fp32) and rwd-7b-q4_0_v2. Deliverables: per-slice p50/p90/p99 latency, token-cost, failure rate, prompt-length CDF, raw traces, and a short marketing-friendly 2-3 line summary per model (we'll paste into slides). Need exact run commands and reproducible seeds. Can runtime do by Friday AM (PST)?

Dev (Runtime): Yep — can run. A couple clarifying q's: 1) Warm vs cold separation? 2) Routing mix: prod proportions or force equal language quotas? 3) Do you want the slide-ready summary to include exact delta numbers or just qualitative "better on short tokens, regressed on very long"?

Lina (Marketing): 1) Separate warm and cold please. Define warm = warmup_tokens=3 and tag with header X-Bench-Warm=1. 2) Use production routing mix but enforce min 1k samples per language so slices aren't tiny. 3) We want exact deltas (numbers) for the slides and a one-line plain-language takeaway. Also include 3-5 representative failure snippets (anonymized) we can show in appendix. Seed for reproducibility: 777777.

Carlos (Eng): FYI: >1024 uses a different kernel path and will change p99/cost. We should log kernel_path and kernel_fallback_count. Also capture tokenizer error codes for failures (so marketing can say "X failures due to tokenization edgecases"). Recommend capping absurdly long sequences at 16k to avoid queue lockups. Suggest concurrency sweep at 4/8/16.

Ravi (Ops): I'll schedule on staging low-priority window 04:30 UTC. Example commands I'll run (will attach job id when queued):

```
./run_bench --model=rwd-7b-v1 --quant=fp32 --samples=10000 --buckets "<32,32-256,256-1024,>1024" --langs "en,es,zh,ar,other" --min_per_lang 1000 --warmup_tokens 3 --warm_header "X-Bench-Warm=1" --concurrency 8 --batch 32 --cap 16384 --seed 777777 --outdir s3://redwood-bench/marketing/5123456789/rwd-7b-v1/ --save-traces --save-csv

./run_bench --model=rwd-7b-q4_0_v2 --quant=q4_0 --samples=10000 --same-flags --outdir s3://redwood-bench/marketing/5123456789/rwd-7b-q4_0_v2/
```
I'll post job ids and link to logs. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Job queued -> jb-20260610-9001. est runtime ~5h. logs: https://ci/internal/jb-20260610-9001/logs

Dev (Runtime): Implementation notes: We'll tag warm requests with header X-Bench-Warm=1. CSVs will have fields: request_id, sample_id, seed, lang, token_count, warm_flag, latency_ms, token_cost, error_code, tokenizer_error, kernel_path. Aggregates will include p50/p90/p99, token-cost-per-response, failure-rate-per-slice, prompt_length_cdf, kernel_fallback_count. We'll also put a small README.txt listing exact git commit of runtime + model artifact sha used. OK?

Lina (Marketing): Perfect. For the failure snippets please redact any PII and replace user text with "[REDACTED]"; keep language and token_count context. Also include a tiny "how we sampled" provenance.txt (SQL + extraction timestamp + seed + sample_ids) so legal can audit later.

Carlos (Eng): One more: please include run-level metadata showing concurrency, batch, GPU type, and observed queue depth percentiles so we can explain any outliers on the slides. I'll add a small script to compute queue-depth from traces if you include the runtime traces.

ci-bot: Job started -> jb-20260610-9001.

ci-bot: Job finished -> jb-20260610-9001. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/marketing/5123456789/. Summary (first-pass):
- rwd-7b-v1 (fp32): <32 p50=12ms p90=28ms p99=110ms; token-cost avg=0.0032; failure_rate overall=0.18% (most in zh >1024)
- rwd-7b-q4_0_v2 (q4_0): <32 p50=10ms p90=26ms p99=130ms; token-cost avg=0.0026; failure_rate overall=0.31% (concentrated on zh long, tokenizer errors)
Notes: q4_0 shows better median on short tokens but regresses on very long sequences; kernel_fallback_count=42 (mostly in zh). Full per-slice CSVs, prompt-length CDFs, traces, provenance.txt, and README.txt are in the bucket.

Ravi (Ops): job ids: jb-20260610-9001 (rwd-7b-v1), jb-20260610-9002 (rwd-7b-q4_0_v2). Logs: https://ci/internal/jb-20260610-9001/logs and https://ci/internal/jb-20260610-9002/logs. Artifacts are immutable; please link to S3 paths in the deck.

Lina (Marketing): This is gold — thank you. Two follow-ups: 1) Can runtime add a one-paragraph non-technical friendly summary per model (2-3 sentences) for the slides? 2) If we want, let's run one short zh-focused follow-up with warmup_tokens=12 to see if failures drop; we'll probably ask later but flagging now.

Dev (Runtime): Will add the 2-3 sentence summary files into each model's outdir (summary.txt). On the zh follow-up, agree it's reasonable — add to backlog and we'll queue low-cost run if you sign off.

Lina (Marketing): Signing off to queue zh follow-up if needed. I'll review CSVs and ping here by EOB with whether we want that follow-up. Thanks team! :raised_hands:
